To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a 1 percentage point increase in real interest rates volatility leads to a 1.2% decrease in output in the short run, a 1.5% decrease in output over the medium run, a 0.5% decrease of consumption over the short run, and a 2% decrease of investment.
a 1% increase in the volatility of real interest rates leads to a 0.4% decline in output in the short run, and a 2% decline in output and investment in the medium run.
an increase in the volatility of real interest rates has a significant negative effect on real variables and the current account.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the real effects of volatility.
the effects on real variables of changes in the volatility in real interest rates.
the effects of volatility shocks in the real interest rate faced by emerging economies and their implications for macroeconomic aggregates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the volatility in the real borrowing costs faced by emerging small open economies matters for their business cycle dynamics.
volatility matters.
volatility in real rates is bad news for small open emerging economies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a rise in volatility is associated with a fall in the welfare of the economy.

a one standard deviation increase in real interest volatility reduces output, consumption, and investment by 0.7, 0.6, and 0.5 percent, respectively, and increases hours worked and the current account by 0.2 and 0.1 percent, respectively.
the effects of volatility shocks on the real economy are quantitatively important.
The main takeaway from our work is that
changes in the volatility process of real interest rates can have a quantitively important effect on real activity.
the real effects of changes in volatility are large, and that they are comparable in magnitude to the real effects of a change in the mean of real interest rates.
the volatility of the interest rate at which emerging small open economies borrow is an important factor in their business cycles.
